thread:
nina: FYI I'm seeing a p95 decode latency increase ~20% on main after last deploy (2026-03-15). Only on long-seq workloads. :eyes:

omar: ugh. Which merge/PR?

nina: looks correlated with merge 2345 — it touched kernel scoring + KV cache steering. Ran a quick perf against canary.

omar: can you paste the perf profile? even a short flame helps.

nina: here — sampled wall time from a short repro (seq=1024):
```
  top functions by self time
  -------------------------
  fused_attention_kernel_selector  34.2%
  kv_prefetch_sync                22.8%
  decode_step_dispatch            18.6%
  kv_evict_scan                   8.9%
  cuda_memcpy_async               6.1%
```

nina: notice the selector and kv_prefetch are much higher than baseline.

tess: PR 2345 changed the kernel scoring to bias for multi-head fused kernels when kv hits are low. Might be flipping choice for long KV-heavy traces.

liam: does this reproduce in CI? perf-ci had a red trend last night.

ci-bot: perf/throughput (daily): main p95_decode +18% vs baseline at 2700110000. See: https://perf.redwood/reports/2700110000

omar: OK bisect plan: run the repro across commits around 2345. I'll try a quick local bisection and report the first bad commit.

omar: quick update — bisect points to commit a7b3d2f (PR 2345) as first bad. Reverting that commit locally restores baseline numbers.

nina: confirmed. Local revert -> p95 back to normal. KV cache hit rates are identical but kernel choice changes on long sequences.

liam: sounds like the scoring heuristic overweights short-seq microbenchmarks and regresses long-seq decode. Can we patch the scoring function to consider average sequence length and kv-cache miss penalty?

omar: small hotfix idea: add a penalty term for estimated KV prefetch cost when seq_len > 512. Patch is small, can test in canary.

nina: also observed more `kv_evict_scan` calls — might be prefetch policy thrashing. Suggest we add a conservative cap on concurrent prefetches for the next rollout.

liam: agree. Two-step mitigation: (1) revert 2345 on prod canary to stop regression, (2) apply patch that adjusts kernel scoring + cap prefetch concurrency, then re-run canary.

oncall-bot: @oncall paging: rollback request submitted for release/2026-03-15 canary.

tess: I'll open an issue with details, link perf graphs, and assign a PR for the scoring tweak.

nina: thanks. tagging @sre for telemetry checks — watch for error spikes while we revert.

liam: timeline — revert canary now, schedule patch PR today, run canary tests. If green, roll forward with scoring tweak and watch p95 for 48h.

omar: I'll post the bisect log + minimal repro in the issue.

nina: sweet. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: action required: revert of commit a7b3d2f scheduled. Perf regression flag cleared on canary after revert (manual verification pending).

nina: leaving steps in the issue. Will follow up with longer traces and kv-metrics tomorrow.

liam: thanks everyone — good catch and fast triage.
